summary: The first detached controller survived. A sandbox process-visibility check incorrectly reported it and its workers absent; archiving live output paths and launching a second controller caused duplicate SMD work and an MSBPG receipt collision.

correction.incorrect_claim: All recorded PIDs were confirmed absent; detached child processes did not survive termination of the exec session.
correction.corrected_fact: An escalated host process-table check on 2026-10-14 showed original controller PID 2644975 alive, PPID 1, with four active MSBPG child workers. Sandboxed process-table visibility was insufficient to establish absence.

smd.evidence: Archived first-attempt worker logs and current second-attempt worker logs each report 2000 completed updates. Current completion receipts identify second-attempt worker PIDs and match current metadata and all saved-plan hashes.
smd.caveat: The two controllers temporarily used overlapping SMD output paths; final current artifacts passed full controller and independent NumPy/POT endpoint audits. Timing is not comparable and is excluded from the scientific comparison.

msbpg.evidence: All four active MSBPG receipts match the current configuration hash, full executed command, source identity, input binding and thread policy. Each worker is a child of the original controller. The second controller stopped before starting any MSBPG worker.

recovery.required: Wait for the original controller and four existing MSBPG workers to settle using host-visible PID identity checks, then independently audit all eight tuning results before selecting, confirming, finalizing and rendering the report.
recovery.reason: Original SMD futures used archived configuration SHA 23b907... and failed after local_config was replaced. The original executor waits for already-queued MSBPG tasks before surfacing that pending failure, so its campaign cannot automatically progress to selection.
recovery.preserve: Keep frozen numerical/controller sources and configuration unchanged, preserve all prior failed-stage and archived evidence, and record recovery under a new wrapper/service.
